title: Tissue Dissociation and Nuclei Isolation
author: Paul Oyler-Castrillo
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bes7jehn
materials: Prepare materials and reagents for the experiment. If there alre multiple people carrying out the experiment, Steps 1.2, 1.3, and 1.4 can be done while someone else carries out Step 2. Step 3 onward will require the NSB (Step 1.2) and NSB+Ruby (Step 1.3) solutions.

Take the suspension and FACS sorting materials to the flow cytometry core for FACS sorting: Nuclei suspension sample(s) 96-well plate or 8-well PCR strip, with BSA (Step 1.4) rich-NSB (Step 1.4) Remaining NSB (to rinse the wells of BSA) Pipettes, pipette tips, and filled ice bucket(s). Proceed to the FACS sorting protocol.

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Reagents
steps.instruction: Set up the centrifuge and prepare the necessary hardware and buffers for the procedure.

substeps.instruction: Pre-chill the centrifuge to 4°C, set to 500 g for 5 min, and set acceleration/deceleration to < 3.
Retrieve tissue samples and keep on dry ice.
Place one 5 mL centrifuge tube on ice per sample.
Set aside 8 mL of EZ Lysis Buffer per sample.
Wash dounce and pestles with 100% EtOH, then RNAse Zap, then 2-3 rounds of RNAse-free water, and finally rinse with EZ Lysis Buffer.
Chill dounce and pestles on ice (e.g., on saran wrap).

steps.title: Prepare Nuclei Suspension Buffer (NSB)
steps.instruction: Prepare the basic Nuclei Suspension Buffer and keep it on ice.

substeps.instruction: For 5 mL of NSB, mix: 5 mL PBS, 25 uL BSA (20 mg/mL), and 25 uL RNase inhibitor (40 U/uL).

steps.title: Prepare Ruby Stain Solution
steps.instruction: If using Vybrant DyeCycle Ruby stain, prepare the staining buffer.

substeps.instruction: Make 1 mL NSB with Ruby at 1:500 dilution per sample.
Add an additional 5 uL/mL RNAse Inhibitor (final concentration: 0.4 U/uL).
If Ruby is not soluble in cold media, dilute it 1:10 in room-temperature NSB first, then 1:50 into cold NSB to achieve the final 1:500 dilution.

steps.title: Prepare Rich-NSB and Collection Plate
steps.instruction: Prepare the high-BSA buffer and the collection vessel for FACS sorting.

substeps.instruction: Prepare rich-NSB per sample (for 50 uL: 50 uL NSB, 2.5 uL RNAse Inhibitor [final 2 U/uL], and 2.5 uL BSA [final 1%]); keep on ice.
Select one 200 uL well per sample (e.g., 8-well PCR strip or 96-well plate) and coat the entire inside with undiluted BSA.
Transport the plate in a clean ziplock bag to the flow cytometry core.
Immediately before sorting, draw off the BSA, rinse the well with basic NSB, and fill with 10-20 uL of rich-NSB (ensuring no bubbles), aiming for a final post-sort volume under 30 uL.

steps.title: Tissue Homogenization and First Digestion Cycle
steps.instruction: Homogenize the tissue and perform the first round of lysis.

substeps.instruction: Transfer tissue to the chilled douncer without allowing it to thaw.
Immediately add 2 mL of ice-cold EZ Lysis Buffer.
Homogenize using 25 strokes of pestle A and 20 strokes of pestle B, raising and lowering slowly to avoid bubbles; keep tissue on ice.
Transfer the suspension to the 5 mL centrifuge tube.
Rinse the douncer with 2 mL ice-cold EZ Lysis Buffer, transfer the rinsate to the tube, and gently mix by inversion.
Incubate on ice for 5 min.
Centrifuge at 500 g for 5 min at 4°C with low acceleration and deceleration.

steps.title: Second Digestion Cycle
steps.instruction: Perform a second round of lysis to further dissociate the tissue.

substeps.instruction: Carefully discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 4 mL ice-cold EZ Lysis Buffer by gentle pipetting.
Incubate on ice for 5 min.
Centrifuge at 500 g for 5 min at 4°C with low acceleration and deceleration.

steps.title: Nuclei Washing and Recovery
steps.instruction: Wash the nuclei to remove lysis buffer and prepare for staining.

substeps.instruction: Carefully discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 4 mL ice-cold Nuclei Suspension Buffer (NSB) by gentle pipetting.
Immediately centrifuge at 500 g for 5 min at 4°C with low acceleration and deceleration.

steps.title: Staining and Filtration
steps.instruction: Stain the nuclei and remove debris using a cell strainer.

substeps.instruction: Pre-wet a 35 um Cell Strainer Cap with ~150-200 um of NSB and keep on ice.
Carefully discard the supernatant from the previous centrifugation.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL ice-cold NSB+Ruby (or ~1.2 mL for large tissue pieces) by gentle pipetting.
Slowly pipette the suspension onto the 35 um Cell Strainer Cap; do not force the liquid through.
If the filter clogs, mix the filtered suspension with the remaining unfiltered suspension, pre-wet a new filter tube, and filter again.
